text:
alex: Thinking out loud — proposing a tiny latency-aware fallback shim for canary/AB that can live at the edge. Decides canary vs stable based on recent p95 + token budget. Wanted opinions on control-plane vs local decisioning.

maria: Love the idea. Main Q: where does the decision live? control-plane policy push or local SDK/agent?

sam: If we do control-plane, cache the decision at the edge with TTL. That avoids per-request hop for most traffic.

rachel: We should keep decisions sticky per session id so we don't flip users mid-request. Also avoid adding RBAC checks per request.

alex: Right. My rough model: control-plane publishes small policy + probes; edge agent runs probes and makes local routing decisions. Control-plane remains authoritative and can force-fallback.

john: Telemetry needs: decision_reason, decision_version, probe_latency_histogram, fallback_count. We also need to persist circuit state (NORMAL/PROBING/DEGRADED) for troubleshooting.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary-policy service v1 rolled out to staging :rocket:

maria: Tradeoffs: control-plane = instant policy changes, but increases control-plane QPS. Edge agents = less load but more moving parts (agents need health and update plumbing).

sam: Combine both: publish policy + sampling seeds; edge agent executes probes and enforces locally with exponential backoff reporting to control-plane. If agent uncertain, fall back to control-plane decision.

alex: Example policy proto (very small):

```
policy {
  p95_threshold_ms: 250
  error_rate_pct: 1.0
  token_budget_per_min: 5000
  sticky_by: "session_id"
  probe_interval_ms: 5000
  fallback_variant: "stable-v2"
}
```

rachel: Edge-agent state machine should be simple: NORMAL -> PROBING -> DEGRADED -> FROZEN (manual override). Keep transitions deterministic and idempotent.

maria: Invariants: (1) No split-brain — control-plane wins when agent is unsure; (2) Rollouts can disable auto-fallback globally; (3) All decisions are logged for replay.

alex: Ops concerns: need an escape hatch flag to disable auto fallback across regions, and ability to pin route for specific tenants. Also add a /canary-policy debug endpoint returning last decision + metrics.

sam: Also add SLO-cost model: prefer fallback when expected user-impact (latency penalty) > model-quality delta. That lets us tune threshold by dollars+latency.

john: Implementation checklist: publish policy proto -> edge-agent subscribes -> control-plane exposes /force-fallback -> tracing hooks and metrics export (sfx + jaeger) -> canary debug UI.

ops-bot: ops-bot: opened RFC tracker https://github.com/redwood/research/issues/1234 with summary + perf experiments :memo:

maria: Next steps: alex to sketch agent proto + minimal control-plane API, sam to prototype probe harness, rachel to write operator runbook for manual overrides.

alex: I'll put a short RFC draft in that issue and add a staging experiment matrix. Thanks for the quick takes :+1:

rachel: Small note — add a limit to how many concurrent fallbacks we can trigger per minute to avoid thrash during noisy neighbor events.

alex: Good call. We'll add "fallback_rate_limit_per_min" to the proto.

sam: Happy to help with a lightweight Go agent; aiming for < 2ms median decision latency when cached.

alex: Awesome, leaving action items on the issue.
